frames.subject: Edda Vale, an ordinary human clinician from the free community of Low Water, a calm capable adult person with an individual simplified angular painted face and hair gathered neatly clear of work. Bone-colored practical waist-and-chest apron over dark civilian work shirt and trousers, sleeves ending at wrists, practical closed worn leather shoes. Apron is a clear broad shape reaching just below the knees with a simple central split for walking and two large flat working pockets. Broad warm brown leather medical satchel at anatomical left hip, viewer right in the front view, secured by a clearly attached diagonal shoulder strap and two simple broad latches. Satchel is closed, no loose bottles or tiny items. A small muted cyan repair patch on one pocket is a personal choice. Two human arms, two human hands, two legs and two shoes, modest ordinary proportions. Both hands remain empty and visibly separate from apron and satchel. Personhood and patient care, not a combat medic or magical healer. No gun, armor, helmet, hat, cowboy accessories, glowing pickup color, recognizable service emblem, cross symbol, military insignia or writing. Keep clothing maintained with only a few broad deliberate repair patches; no dirty photographic long coat, dramatic damage or busy medical clutter. Proposed face only, not an established age, ethnicity or voice.
